newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Senior economist sees IMF-Russia deal on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Senior economist sees IMF-Russia deal on Friday.

text.p: The World Bank's former chief economist in Moscow said on Thursday he expected Russia and the International Monetary Fund to sign an economic plan for 1997 on Friday.
"My expectation... is that the IMF deal is going to be completed tomorrow," said Charles Blitzer, Emerging Markets, Europe, Chief Economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette investment bank in London.
Russia must agree a plan for the IMF to continue disbursements of its three-year $10 billion loan to Russia.
"I don't have the text of the IMF agreement, but my understanding is that the text is consistent with the written text of the president's speech last week," he said.
Blitzer, who left the World Bank in early 1996, said the pro-reform speech by President Boris Yeltsin was a "sea change" from past speeches.
Blitzer predicted Russia would see two percent gross domestic product growth in 1997, in line with Russian government forecasts.
